rule: A basis remains a live fundamental candidate only if it has a residual beyond the strongest parent formalism in expressivity, developmental semantics, or resource-bounded prediction. Representation-only differences do not suffice.

candidates.reason: Any frozen finite deterministic network of finite local adaptive units plus finite topology state flattens exactly to one finite-state transducer.
Parameterized maps plus update/request structure already have mature compositional theories. Calling them a new cognitive atom would reinvent those parents.
surviving_questions: non-neural/probabilistic/programmatic developmental compilation without black-box morphisms

candidates.reason: A sufficiently expressive rewritable program graph can encode essentially any morphology, but this alone predicts neither learnability nor morphology emergence.
surviving_questions: restricted typed sublanguages with nontrivial compilation bounds

candidates.reason: Stochastic generative composition is already a mature formal object. Treating deterministic systems as degenerate distributions does not explain morphology differences.
surviving_questions: whether stochasticity is resource-irreducible under bounded simulation
developmental compilation into/out of deterministic forms

programme_conclusion: No current candidate deserves the title fundamental cognitive unit. The next useful object is likely a resource-bounded equivalence class of adaptive factorizations plus morphogenesis/update laws, not a named architecture primitive.
